Value: Edge of cloth folded and sewn to prevent unravelling; also used to adjust garment length
Allowed Wording: Wikipedia defines a hem as a finish in which the edge of the cloth is folded and sewn to stop it unraveling, and notes hems also set garment length
Notes: Reference work, not primary; general definition only

Value: Double-folded, overlocked and folded, rolled, bias tape, blind
Allowed Wording: Wikipedia names double-folded, overlocked and folded, rolled, bias tape and blind hems among common types

Value: Trim hem to 5/8 in; fold raw edge under 1/8 in; press; topstitch near fold, then a second parallel row
Allowed Wording: NMSU Extension describes trimming a woven hem allowance to 5/8 inch, turning the raw edge under 1/8 inch and pressing before topstitching

Value: Trim hem to 1/2 in; skip the 1/8 in turn-under
Allowed Wording: For knits, NMSU Extension trims the allowance to 1/2 inch and skips the 1/8 inch turn-under

Value: Trim to 1 1/4 in; fold raw edge under 1/4 in; press; stitch one row near upper edge and a second row 1/4 in below
Allowed Wording: NMSU Extension's topstitched hem uses a 1 1/4 inch allowance with the raw edge turned under 1/4 inch
Notes: Light- to medium-weight wovens and knits

Value: Trim allowance to 5/8 in; press on hemline; stitch on fold line with narrow close zigzag about 1/8 in wide; press with damp cloth
Allowed Wording: NMSU Extension suggests a narrow, close zigzag about 1/8 inch wide for stretchable knits such as jersey

Value: Topstitching stitch length slightly longer than regular stitching
Allowed Wording: NMSU Extension advises a stitch length slightly longer than regular for topstitched knit hems
Notes: No numeric length given by source

Claim: Presser feet that save hemming time
Value: Blind hem foot and rolled hem foot
Allowed Wording: NMSU Extension lists the blind hem foot and rolled hem foot as feet that can cut down on sewing time

Value: Blind stitch foot; tension Auto; regular blind stitch for firm fabric, elastic blind stitch for soft stretchable fabric; stitching nearly invisible on the right side; make a sewing test first
Allowed Wording: Singer's help page pairs the blind stitch foot with a regular blind stitch for firm fabrics and an elastic one for soft, stretchable fabrics, and says to sew a test first

Claim: Preparing the raw edge before a blind hem
Value: Turn raw edge under on fine fabrics; overcast on medium to heavyweight fabrics; then turn up the hem, press and pin
Allowed Wording: Singer's help page says to turn the raw edge under on fine fabrics or overcast it on medium to heavyweight ones, then turn up, press and pin the hem

Value: Do a trial sewing first with fabric and thread matching the project; use the presser foot the machine indicates
Allowed Wording: Brother's manual advises a trial sewing with fabric and thread that match the project before starting
